title: Fibre restriction of the proper-support pullback map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Let
$$X'\xrightarrow{a}X,\; f'\downarrow,\; f\downarrow,\; Y'\xrightarrow{b}Y$$
be a Cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product], with $f$ separated and locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use direct image and constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Suppose $G\subseteq f_*F$ and $H\subseteq f'_*a^{-1}F$ are subsheaves with the following section descriptions. For every etale $U\to Y$, $G(U)$ consists of the sections of $F(X\times_YU)$ whose closed support is proper over $U$; for every etale $V\to Y'$, $H(V)$ consists of the sections of $(a^{-1}F)(X'\times_{Y'}V)$ whose closed support is proper over $V$. Here support is the locus of nonzero geometric germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and a closed subset is proper over its base if its reduced induced closed subscheme is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].
Let $\alpha:G\to b_*H$ be the section-pullback morphism of [lem-cbc-proper-support-pullback-section-map], and let $\beta:b^{-1}G\to H$ be its adjunct. For a geometric point $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar y=b\bar y'$. Write $\rho_G$ and $\rho_H$ for the restriction isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk] from $G_{\bar y}$ and $H_{\bar y'}$ to the modules of fibre sections whose closed support is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Let
$$c:(b^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\bar y}$$
be the germ-compatible inverse-image stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The square is Cartesian, so it identifies $X'_{\bar y'}$ with $X_{\bar y}$; inverse-image composition identifies their coefficient sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Under these identifications the following equality of maps to the same module of properly supported fibre sections holds:
$$\rho_H\circ\beta_{\bar y'}=\rho_G\circ c.$$
More explicitly, for every pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar y$ and $s\in G(U)$, both sides send the germ of the unit pullback of $s$ on $U\times_YY'$ to the restriction of $s$ along $X_{\bar y}\to X\times_YU$.

proof.text: Fix a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar y$ and $s\in G(U)$. Put $V=U\times_Y Y'$ with marked point $(\bar u,\bar y')$, $t=\eta_{b,G}(U)(s)\in(b^{-1}G)(V)$, and $z=\operatorname{germ}_{\bar y'}(t)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], $c(z)=\operatorname{germ}_{\bar y}(s)$. Apply that abelian-sheaf statement to the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$: [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], clauses (2) and (3), identifies the module inverse image and its unit with the abelian ones. The normalization in [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk] therefore gives $(\rho_G\circ c)(z)=s|_{X_{\bar y}}$.

proof.text: The adjunction $b^{-1}\dashv b_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives $b_*\beta\circ\eta_{b,G}=\alpha$, since $\beta$ is the adjunct of $\alpha$. This is the defining unit equation for adjuncts. Its component at $U$ reads $\beta_V(t)=\alpha_U(s)$; the component of $b_*\beta$ at $U$ is precisely $\beta_V$. The module adjunction has the same unit by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], clause (3). By [lem-cbc-proper-support-pullback-section-map], the section $\alpha_U(s)\in H(V)$ is the unit pullback of $s$ on $W'=X'\times_{Y'}V\cong(X\times_YU)\times_YY'$. Thus $\beta_{\bar y'}(z)$ is the germ of this explicitly specified section.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_YU$, $Z=X_{\bar y}$, $Z'=X'_{\bar y'}$, and let $d:Z'\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ be the canonical fibre isomorphism. Let $q:W'\to W$ be the projection, $r:Z\to W$ the lift defined by $\bar u$, and $r':Z'\to W'$ the lift defined by $(\bar u,\bar y')$. Their projections give $q\circ r'=r\circ d$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The restriction normalization of [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk] sends the germ from step 2 to $(\alpha_U(s))|_{Z'}$. Write $i':Z'\to X'$ and $i:Z\to X$ for the fibre projections. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] sends the iterated unit pullback $i'^*(a^*s)$ to $(a\circ i')^*s$. Restrict this equality along the marked lift to the pullback of the etale object $W$; clause (0) permits these restrictions. Since $a\circ i'=i\circ d$ and $q\circ r'=r\circ d$, the resulting section is exactly the pullback by $d$ of $s|_Z$. The set-level equality applies to our coefficients: [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], clauses (2) and (3), identifies underlying abelian inverse images and their units with the set ones, and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], clauses (2) and (3), does the same for modules. After the coefficient and fibre identifications in the statement, $(\rho_H\circ\beta_{\bar y'})(z)=s|_Z$.

proof.text: The computations in steps 1 and 3 prove the requested explicit formula for every $U,\bar u,s$. They give equality in the submodule of properly supported fibre sections: both expressions lie there by the specified codomains of $\rho_G,\rho_H$, and equality of their underlying sections is equality in that submodule. To obtain equality of maps, precompose both maps with $c^{-1}$ and then with every canonical map $G(U)\to G_{\bar y}$. Step 1 identifies $c^{-1}(\operatorname{germ}_{\bar y}s)$ with the $z$ used above, so these composites agree. By the colimit definition of the stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], maps out of $G_{\bar y}$ are determined by all these canonical maps. The composites with $c^{-1}$ are equal; cancel this isomorphism to get $\rho_H\circ\beta_{\bar y'}=\rho_G\circ c$.
